messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For French, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement (French morphosyntax) | |-------------|----------------------|------------------------------------------| | **Ahi** | Interjection of emotional intensity | **Interjection** “Ah !” – exclamative particle. *Back‑translation check:* “Ah!” | | **quanto** | Degree adverb marking intensity (“how hard”) – not a binary comparison | **Adverbial phrase** “à quel point” (introduces a scalar degree). Must preserve upward direction (greater difficulty). *Back‑translation check:* “how” | | **a** | Preposition introducing infinitive complement of “tell” | **Preposition** “de” (governing infinitive). *Back‑translation check:* “to” | | **dir** | Infinitive verb “to tell” (act of expressing) | **Infinitive verb** “dire”. *Back‑translation check:* “tell” | | **qual** | Interrogative/relative pronoun introducing content clause “what … was” | **Relative pronoun** “ce que” (introduces embedded question). *Back‑translation check:* “what” | | **era** | Imperfect indicative of “to be” (past state) | **Imperfect indicative** “était” (3rd sg.). *Back‑translation check:* “was” | | **è** | Present indicative of “to be” (identifies “thing”) | **Present indicative** “est” (3rd sg.). *Back‑translation check:* “is” | | **cosa** | Abstract noun “thing” (subject complement) | **Noun** “chose” (fem., singular) with copular construction. *Back‑translation check:* “thing” | | **dura** | Predicate adjective “hard” (qualifies “thing”) | **Adjective** “dure” agreeing in gender/number with “chose”. *Back‑translation check:* “hard” | | **esta** | Demonstrative adjective “this” (points to wood) | **Demonstrative adjective** “cette” (fem., singular) agreeing with “forêt”. *Back‑translation check:* “this” | | **selva** | Common noun “wood/forest” (head of NP) | **Noun** “forêt” (fem., singular). *Back‑translation check:* “wood” | | **selvaggia** | Attributive adjective “wild” | **Adjective** “sauvage” agreeing with “forêt”. *Back‑translation check:* “wild” | | **e** (first) | Coordinating conjunction linking adjectives | **Coordinating conjunction** “et”. *Back‑translation check:* “and” | | **aspra** | Attributive adjective “rough” | **Adjective** “âpre” agreeing with “forêt”. *Back‑translation check:* “rough” | | **e** (second) | Coordinating conjunction linking adjectives | **Coordinating conjunction** “et”. *Back‑translation check:* “and” | | **forte** | Attributive adjective “dense/strong” | **Adjective** “dense” (or “solide”) agreeing with “forêt”. *Back‑translation check:* “dense” | | **che** | Relative pronoun “which” introducing clause | **Relative pronoun** “qui” (refers to “forêt”). *Back‑translation check:* “which” | | **nel** | Contraction of “in” + “the” (preposition + article) | **Prepositional phrase** “dans le” (introduces location of mental act). *Back‑translation check:* “in the” | | **pensier** | Poetic form of “thought” (object of preposition) | **Noun** “pensée” (fem., singular) as object of “dans le”. *Back‑translation check:* “thought” | | **rinova** | Present indicative “renews” (causal action) | **Present indicative verb** “renouvelle” (3rd sg.) – causal, iterative. *Back‑translation check:* “renews” | | **la** | Definite article marking “fear” | **Definite article** “la” (fem., singular) preceding “peur”. *Back‑translation check:* “the” | | **paura** | Noun “fear” (direct object) | **Noun** “peur” (fem., singular) as direct object of “renouvelle”. *Back‑translation check:* “fear” |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable French components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 4: Ah à quel point il est difficile de dire ce que était est chose dure / Ah à quel point de dire ce que était est chose dure / Ah à quel point il est dur de dire ce que était est chose dure - Line 5: cette forêt sauvage et âpre et dense / cette forêt sauvage âpre et dense / cette forêt sauvage et dense et âpre - Line 6: qui dans la pensée renouvelle la peur / qui renouvelle la peur dans la pensée / qui la peur renouvelle dans la pensée

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into French lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

Source Line: 4 Ahi quanto a dir qual era è cosa dura Line Inventory: - Ah à quel point il est difficile de dire ce que était est chose dure Assembly Notes: - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase already contains the interjection, degree expression, infinitival complement, and predicate. Target Text: Ah à quel point il est difficile de dire ce que était est chose dure
Source Line: 5 esta selva selvaggia e aspra e forte Line Inventory: - cette forêt sauvage et âpre et dense Assembly Notes: - Phrase is a complete noun phrase matching the source predicate; no extra words required. Target Text: cette forêt sauvage et âpre et dense
Source Line: 6 che nel pensier rinova la paura! Line Inventory: - qui dans la pensée renouvelle la peur Assembly Notes: - Added the exclamation mark from the source line; no other insertions needed. Target Text: qui dans la pensée renouvelle la peur!

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 4 - Target Text (from Step 4): Ah à quel point il est difficile de dire ce que était chose dure - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): Ah how much it is difficult to say what was thing hard - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): Ah! how hard a thing it is to tell what … was - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 5 - Target Text (from Step 4): cette forêt sauvage et âpre et dense - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): this forest wild and rough and dense - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): this wild and rough and dense wood - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 6 - Target Text (from Step 4): qui dans la pensée renouvelle la peur! - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): which in the thought renews the fear! - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): which in thought renews the fear! - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
All lines pass verification.
```text Ah à quel point il est difficile de dire ce que était chose dure cette forêt sauvage et âpre et dense qui dans la pensée renouvelle la peur! ```
